section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that there are two types of miracles: a change in the form and nature of creations, and a change in their very material existence, each enabled by the corresponding nullification of the creation.
section.t: And this is that in miracles there are two types,
a change in the form and nature of creations
(like the splitting of the Sea of Reeds where the waters stood like a wall)
and a change in the very existence of their material substance
(like the miracle that the water turned to blood and that the staff turned into a serpent),
for through the nullification that is in the form of creations
(for the coming into being of form is from the Will)
they are like vessels for the miracle of change of form and nature,
and through the nullification that is in their very existence
(for the coming into being of their existence has no place in intellect)
they are like vessels for the miracle of change of their very existence.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that conversely, for the supernal to be drawn into the natural world, there must be a parallel of nature within the supernal, which is why the blessing mentions multiple types of miracles.
section.t: And it may be said,
that correspondingly it is on the other side,
that in order for that which is above nature to be drawn into the nature of the world,
it is through that which is above nature having a likeness of nature.
And this is "Blessed is He Who performed miracles" in the plural,
a multiplicity of types of miracles,
for it may be said that from the reasons that there are a multiplicity of miracles,
even though the matter of multiplicity
(division)
is in the chain of descent and the root which is above nature is above the chain of descent,
it is in order that through this it will be possible for the drawing down of that which is above nature into the nature of the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two general categories of miracles as taught by the Rebbe Rashab: miracles above nature and miracles clothed in natural ways, with further subdivisions regarding how the natural garment reveals or conceals the miracle.
section.t: And the matter of the multiplicity of types in miracles is explained by the Rebbe
(Moharashab)
of blessed memory in the maamar,
that in general they are divided into two types33.
Miracles that are above nature,
and miracles that are clothed in natural ways.
And in particular,
even within the miracles that are clothed in nature itself there are two types.
The garments of nature are in a manner that it is recognizable in them that they are only a garment for the miracle that is clothed in them,
like the miracles of Chanukah and Purim
(and likewise the miracles of the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev and Yud Beis Tammuz)
that despite their being clothed in natural ways,
nevertheless the miracle within them was revealed and apparent
(to the extent that all the ends of the earth saw)
the miracle within them.
And the garments of nature conceal and hide the miracle that is clothed in them.
To the extent that sometimes they conceal and hide it completely,
so that it is not at all recognizable that it is a miracle,
"the master of the miracle does not recognize his miracle"34.
